title: The restarted work block
hook: A toy session pays the same startup cost each time work resumes. How much fits?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Account for how chunk duration changes the fraction spent on a repeated startup cost.

misconception: Splitting work into shorter chunks leaves the same usable work if total session time stays fixed.
objective: Account for how chunk duration changes the fraction spent on a repeated startup cost.

claims.text: The named work is Peopleware, by Tom DeMarco and Timothy Lister, candidate publication year 1987.
claims.source: Tom DeMarco and Timothy Lister, Peopleware (1987); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Peopleware treats interruptions and the working environment as relevant to software work.
claims.source: Tom DeMarco and Timothy Lister, Peopleware (1987); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated intervals model: A inputs [60, 20, 10] yield 40; B inputs [60, 10, 10] yield 30. Prediction correct option 30. A yields {A} work minutes; B {B}. Shorter chunks repeat the same ten-minute startup more often, leaving a larger share of the hour outside work. The startup cost is invented and constant, not a measured cognitive recovery time.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy session lasts 48 minutes; each chunk is 8 work plus 4 startup minutes. Finished work minutes? Four complete 12-minute cycles fit, and each contains eight work minutes: 32 total.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, intervals, inputs [48, 8, 4], output 32; independent Python recomputation.

claims.text: Does it hold up? The arithmetic follows our assumptions; real-world applicability and book attribution remain unverified.
claims.source: Scope limitation, not a research verdict: only original toy derivation supplied. Publication requires independently opened book chapter and separate real-world evidence review; no effectiveness inference is made.
